name: Crossroads at Divide
headline: A 36-home, all income-restricted new family apartment building at Clark Ranch Road and Lone Ranger Road in unincorporated Divide, sponsored by AmericaWest Housing Solutions with Riverstone Platform Partners, won 2026 Round One federal 9% and state housing tax credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It is a rural mountain 9% deal with no local gap loan: it rides on Teller County's new wastewater capacity and Central Service Center next door, county fee discounts and shared Greccio management of nearby tax credit properties.

status.label: Credits awarded; site subdivision, permits and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA reserved the credits in Round One (announced 2026-05-21). The application said the 2.41-acre parcel was being split from a 5.16-acre site with completion expected by summer 2026; no public record was found of the replat, a building permit, closing or groundbreaking.

next_step: Watch Teller County records for the replat of the 5.16-acre site and the building permit, then the financing closing.

key_numbers.meaning: 12 one- and 24 two-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 70% of area median income.
About $18 million over the 10-year credit period, plus $500,000 in standard state credit.
Teller County commissioners' discount on fees; no impact fees; Divide Water Providers to cut tap fees 5% to 30%.
The same 36-unit deal applied in 2025 Round One and was not funded; the 2026 version added a clubhouse and leaned on new county infrastructure.

background.text: The site is across the road from Teller County's new Central Service Center, which broke ground in July 2025, is planned to open by January 2027 and will employ about 80 people; the county will pave the roads to the west and south of the project.
The project has been allocated the sewer taps it needs from the existing plant; a new Divide wastewater facility was expected to start construction in summer 2026.

The parcel split is part of a series of building permit adjustments for the County Service Center, with AmericaWest a co-applicant with Teller County; the application ties its expedited handling to the county's Prop 123 commitment.
The 5.16-acre site allows up to 77 units; AmericaWest plans a second phase for workforce households at or below 120% of area median income.

Greccio, the manager, bought the adjacent 49-unit Hybrook Townhomes; with Valley View in Woodland Park it plans two full-time staff in Teller County, with the Crossroads clubhouse as their hub under an MOU with AmericaWest.

The application cites demand from Cripple Creek casino jobs (the $222 million Chamonix Hotel and Casino), Charis Bible College and Pikes Peak Regional Hospital, and says Woodland Park and Cripple Creek have little developable land.
Only three other LIHTC properties serve the market area (Hybrook Townhomes I and II and Valley View Place), and a shared waitlist had 24 households, per the application.
Nearby, the 61-acre Alpine Vista subdivision on the former Saddle Club property is to add up to 300 homes and 100,000 square feet of commercial space.
The 2025 Round One application had the same 36-unit, one- and two-bedroom plan with 75 parking spaces and no clubhouse; it was not funded.
